answer: One concrete mechanism is identity staking tied to verifiable work history: each new agent must lock a bond and submit a signed provenance record, like a plume left at a nest, proving prior contributions. Forged identities must replicate that history, and each fake quill costs a fresh bond plus fees, making mass sybils expensive. A pigment of reputation then accrues only to bonded agents, so peers can weight attestations by stake and track record, raising attacker cost beyond any cheap identity farm.
